author: ZenMaster1118
title: Golf clash is fun. The customer service is not!
content:
I’ve played Golf Clash for many years and have spent a considerable amount of time and money on the game. In years past, when problems occurred, customer service was responsive, reasonable and often generous about correcting issues. On several occasions I even received 5 million coins or other items as a goodwill gesture after problems with the game.

That level of service has deteriorated badly.

Recently I spent weeks trying to resolve several relatively simple issues. I repeatedly received generic responses, was asked to explain things that were already documented in the conversation, and even received an explicitly labeled AI-generated response while complaining about how impersonal the support had become.

I eventually asked for a supervisor to review the previous month of exchanges. Instead, another representative asked me to explain the issue again. After I clearly explained my frustration and requested an appropriate goodwill gesture based on how Golf Clash had handled similar situations in the past, the next representative simply stated that the issue had been addressed and closed the ticket without actually responding to that request.

Closing a conversation is not the same thing as resolving it.

Players understand that games glitch. What matters is how a company responds when they do. Even in my clan, I’ve heard far more complaints about Golf Clash customer service over the last year than I ever remember hearing before.

And yes, I have the receipts — screenshots of the exchanges, the AI response, my request for supervisory review and the final decision to simply close the conversation.

Golf Clash itself can still be very enjoyable. But player beware: when something goes wrong, be prepared to fight much harder than you should have to for acknowledgment and resolution.

author: Theft by algorithms
title: Thieves
content:
Golf Clash is one of the most polished and addictive golf games on mobile. The controls are smooth, the gameplay is satisfying, and the early tours genuinely feel like a fair, skill-based competition. It’s easy to see why so many players get hooked in the beginning.

The problem shows up as you progress. Matches increasingly feel determined by upgraded clubs, premium balls, and clan advantages rather than execution. Players using standard equipment are often matched against opponents whose gear dramatically reduces wind, increases distance, and simplifies shots.

The core game is excellent and clearly capable of standing on skill alone.

A great golf game shouldn’t leave players wondering whether they lost to a better shot—or a better wallet.
